claims.text: Greg Short asserts that investors want to see authentic, slightly eccentric entrepreneurs rather than polished conformists, and that authenticity does not impede fundraising; he raised $100M while dressed casually (Air Force Ones, cargo pants) rather than in conventional business attire.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
bounded_by: Speaker notes he was groomed and had himself together — authenticity does not mean appearing unkempt

claims.text: Greg Short asserts that founders who adopt a conformist, status-quo persona (the mannequin or NPC archetype) unnecessarily trade away the competitive differentiation that personal authenticity provides; being a recognizable one-of-one identity is available to anyone willing to reject social conformity pressure.
claims.speaker: Greg Short

examples.text: Greg Short raised $100M in funding while wearing Air Force Ones and cargo pants throughout the process. He was groomed and presentable but dressed as himself rather than in conventional business attire, using this as evidence that investor audiences respond to authentic personal identity rather than the polished conformist look entrepreneurs often assume is required.

practices.text: Embrace your authentic appearance and personality in investor and public-facing contexts rather than adopting a generic professional persona.
